whatItFakes: A month without a supplied housing event contributes zero event effect.
why: The standalone rule accepts only supplied events and needs a neutral result when none is present.
replacement: A sourced, recorded housing-event effect for every macro month.

whatItFakes: The layoff rule permits a one-dollar annual pay-coverage tolerance.
why: The legacy comparison includes this tolerance and golden equivalence retains it.
replacement: A sourced accounting or payroll tolerance for the modeled books.

whatItFakes: Missing town-average pay contributes zero to the hiring threshold.
why: The legacy helper defaults to zero when its caller has no town-pay record.
replacement: A recorded town-average pay amount or a tagged estimate for the relevant place.

whatItFakes: Persisted macro values retain six decimal places.
why: The port preserves legacy replay precision until a persisted-data precision contract is set.
replacement: A documented precision contract for macro values.

whatItFakes: Home-purchase prices round to $1,000 increments.
why: The legacy purchase calculation rounds this way for replay equivalence.
replacement: A sourced purchase-pricing and currency-rounding policy.

whatItFakes: New hires start at the 25th wage percentile and reach the 75th after 20 years.
why: The legacy rule has no sourced tenure curve and these values preserve current behavior.
replacement: A measured tenure-to-wage progression by occupation and place.

whatItFakes: The lifted job-rate rule accepts caller-supplied federal/state floor data; local floors are not represented.
why: The current source reader supplies no local minimum-wage data.
replacement: Place and effective-date keyed local minimum-wage facts.

whatItFakes: Policy-rate midpoint stands in for a 30-year mortgage-rate change.
why: The available macro records do not contain a consistent mortgage-rate series for every modeled place and month.
replacement: A supplied monthly mortgage-rate series for each place.

whatItFakes: Home-price growth has no housing-supply response term.
why: A place-level housing-supply elasticity is not present in the supplied facts.
replacement: A sourced supply-elasticity fact and its measured pass-through coefficient.

whatItFakes: The first recorded home-price index starts at 1.
why: The pure rule receives a finite macro series and needs a deterministic initial index.
replacement: A supplied, source-backed opening index level and date.

whatItFakes: Eviction disposition uses a four-month counsel threshold and a two-month threshold for a lenient judge.
why: The legacy disposition rule has no jurisdiction-specific outcome records; both are estimates retained for golden equivalence.
replacement: A sourced jurisdiction-specific case-outcome model with counsel and judge facts.

whatItFakes: Home-purchase financing uses a 360-month fixed term.
why: The legacy purchase rule uses this term and has no buyer-selected term fact.
replacement: A recorded loan term or sourced term distribution for the buyer and loan type.

whatItFakes: Banks do not extend new credit when national credit tightness is 0.75 or higher.
why: The legacy bank rule pauses new lines and growth after a national tightening threshold.
replacement: A sourced lender-wide credit availability measure and place-level applicability rule.

whatItFakes: A business borrows from the open town bank with the largest deposits; deposit ties use bank ID order.
why: Individual business-bank relationships are not supplied to the selection rule.
replacement: A recorded business-to-bank relationship and its active loan terms.

whatItFakes: A household head aged 60 or older selects owned outright tenure for a newly chosen home.
why: The legacy home selector uses age as a proxy and receives no recorded mortgage balance or paid-off status.
replacement: The household's recorded loan balance and home equity at the move date.

whatItFakes: Households of up to two select an apartment fallback; households of five or more may select a large house.
why: The legacy home selector uses fixed household-size bands without a sourced household-space model.
replacement: A household-space model fitted to recorded resident, room and dwelling facts.

whatItFakes: When a town spans multiple counties, its private employment mix weights each available county equally.
why: The legacy mix does not use town job counts or county-level town shares to weight county records.
replacement: Recorded place-level jobs or a sourced county-to-town employment allocation.

whatItFakes: Payroll aggregation considers late-recorded transfers only within 45 days before the selected period.
why: The legacy reader stops once it reaches outcomes older than its 45-day lookback.
replacement: A sourced, recorded payroll-transfer posting-lag distribution.

whatItFakes: Rejects operations when an intermediate product exceeds safe integer precision even when the final rational result or comparison could be represented.
why: Legacy uses Number intermediates. Preserve its overflow errors instead of silently adopting BigInt.
replacement: Reviewed exact-integer arithmetic with an explicit persisted quantity bound.

whatItFakes: One-person households take a studio; other households use two people per bedroom, capped at four.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Recorded dwelling capacity/bedrooms and applicable occupancy rules.

whatItFakes: Subtracts 1e-9 before rounding the recorded affordable-home obligation upward.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Reviewed exact-ratio adopted obligation and rounding contract.

whatItFakes: Multiplies a household-size mean by a region/national mean ratio as a joint cost estimate.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Sourced household-size-by-region joint expenditure records.

whatItFakes: Business operating income uses receipts less payroll and omits other operating costs.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Recorded completed operating expenses alongside payroll and receipts.

whatItFakes: Weekly pay closes Friday, semimonthly pay on the 15th/month end, and biweekly phases anchor January 7, 2000.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Recorded employer-specific pay calendars, holiday and posting conventions.

whatItFakes: Object.entries checks supplied source values but missing required source keys can pass unchecked.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Reviewed explicit presence check for each required source role.

whatItFakes: Macro anchors, persistence, era responses and signed-shock magnitudes retain native director-authored provisional coefficients.
why: The native section-13 model is not a fitted forecast; the frozen startup/month contract must not be silently recalibrated during the lift.
replacement: Admitted versioned macro response parameters with source and calibration evidence.

whatItFakes: Unemployment retains the native 0.985 monthly gap retention read from one 2009–2012 national episode.
why: One episode is an estimate, not an independently fitted all-place recovery relationship.
replacement: Reviewed multi-episode unemployment response and persisted policy version.

whatItFakes: National credit starts and responds through the native mixed sourced/estimated debt, capital, repricing, loss, burden and demand coefficients.
why: BIS/FRED debt observations and NBER calibration citations do not make all response coefficients measured; the aggregate model is preserved.
replacement: Admitted dated credit stocks and empirically checked response parameters with declared uncertainty.

whatItFakes: Rate concerns retain ordinal gap bands, one-step trait shifts and native preferred moves and explanation text.
why: These are authored individual judgment estimates passed to the existing actor chooser, not a new chooser or measured decision probabilities.
replacement: Admitted central-bank judgment model and English-engine realization of its records.

whatItFakes: A decayed intensity below 0.01 stops contributing to the monthly macro impulse.
why: Native numerical cutoff changes a small continuous impulse to zero; the lift preserves the cutoff unchanged.
replacement: Reviewed decay precision/termination policy and model version.

whatItFakes: Local macro shocks use the national-average exposure multiplier 1 and national price/credit readings.
why: No compiled local sector exposure or local price stock is read by the native model.
replacement: Sourced local-sector exposure and recorded local price/credit conditions.

whatItFakes: National housing supply/demand ratio holds its previous or opening value while construction/migration stocks are absent.
why: The native month has no housing stock producer; no absent stock is invented by this rule lift.
replacement: Separate recorded housing-stock producer and admitted aggregate ratio math.

whatItFakes: Reserve presidents retire at the qualifying five-year February term end and successors use a uniform 90-day interval.
why: The native age/term policy is retained; the succession interval is a game profile rather than bank-specific evidence.
replacement: Dated bank-specific succession/approval records and admitted transition timing.

whatItFakes: Working normal unemployment averages up to 240 releases once 60 are present; otherwise it uses 4.4 percent.
why: The native minimum and lookback/fallback are authored policy assumptions, not a measured changing natural rate for each committee.
replacement: Admitted real-time normal-rate estimate with dated source vintage and uncertainty.

whatItFakes: Dissent counts opposite signs, so same-direction different-size preferences do not dissent; a controlled nonpresiding member with no recorded choice still counts in the majority denominator.
why: These native vote semantics are preserved as a model/suspected defect, not repaired; the lift makes no ordinary production-defect claim.
replacement: Reviewed recorded member votes including proposed magnitude and explicit player abstention/choice semantics.

whatItFakes: Actor requests and the policy-rate event retain unchanged native option labels, reasons and summary realization.
why: KEEP decision math travels here with exact caller output; separate English realization is not invented during this lift.
replacement: English-engine realization from the admitted consideration and event records.

whatItFakes: Housing ratio below 0.98 or above 1.02 is described as shortage or surplus.
why: These are native authored display bands around neutral ratio 1, not sourced housing-stock classification thresholds.
replacement: Admitted sourced housing reading/classification policy.

whatItFakes: Town establishment, staff and sales means use population scaling and land shares, with state/national source fallbacks.
why: Retains native CBP/Economic Census projection, not observed town transactions.
replacement: Admitted dated town business census and uncertainty.

whatItFakes: A multi-county place takes the unweighted mean of county home-value medians; missing county values use state/national medians.
why: The native surrogate median is retained unchanged, not repaired into a population or dwelling weighted value.
replacement: Admitted local dwelling-price distribution with dated coverage.

whatItFakes: Missing guideline years use the prior/first row; added-person Alaska/Hawaii amounts scale the contiguous amount by the one-person ratio.
why: These native extrapolations are retained; unsupported regional/year rules are not researched during the lift.
replacement: Complete dated HHS guidelines for all applicable places and sizes.

whatItFakes: Active comparable USD agreements are averaged after weekly-hours and cadence normalization, preferring local agreements.
why: Retains native average-pay estimate and its English note; contracts are not observed individual future earnings.
replacement: Admitted comparable earnings distribution and separate English realization.

whatItFakes: Industry/public employment is allocated to representative workplaces using authored share tables and national fallback rows.
why: The native workplace weights are game assumptions retained with the county/state source selector.
replacement: Researched occupation/industry/place workplace distributions.

whatItFakes: Opening plans cap at two establishments per kind and three workers, and add one likeliest business when all projected counts round to zero.
why: Native opening representativeness limits and minimum-employer assumption are retained.
replacement: Admitted opening population/business coverage policy.

whatItFakes: A modeled bank uses the observed asset row nearest its modeled deposits; fewer than five own-state rows use the national pool.
why: Retains native deposits-to-assets profile surrogate and fallback; no ratio recalibration.
replacement: Admitted dated bank-specific balance sheet or modeled profile policy.

whatItFakes: SCF family transaction-account median shares interpolate in log income and clamp to end rows.
why: Retains a family-table proxy for individual modeled opening cash.
replacement: Admitted individual household cash distribution with dated uncertainty.

whatItFakes: All dates use the retained 2026-27 undergraduate rate; outside the award window it remains labeled estimated.
why: Native snippet-derived nearest-row behavior is preserved.
replacement: Complete sourced award-year and program rate table.
